framework_detected: In Medias Res with a flash-back ('45 MINUTES EARLIER' at 5 s) into a PAS chain; executed fully on the problem side (cold open, rewind, three escalating 'Done.' beats, return to the stalled Send at 41.6-46 s) but the 'proof and roadmap' part arrives only at 46 s, so the hook carries 45 s of pain with no promise of relief.
framework_recommended: In Medias Res is right for this buyer (a concrete number mismatch minutes before a board meeting), but it should be fused with a Delayed-Gratification promise in the first 5 s: one line or frame that says the film will show how the mismatch gets caught, so the 40 s problem run reads as setup rather than a complaint montage.

hook_alternatives.first_3s_visual: Real laptop in a dark room, cursor hovering over Send, a red 8:59 clock; the two cards €74.6m vs €71–73m slam onto the screen
hook_alternatives.line: One minute to the board. Two numbers. Which one is right?
hook_alternatives.why: Puts a human hand on the Send button at frame 1 (real footage, not a flat UI) and makes the stakes a decision the viewer wants answered.

hook_alternatives.first_3s_visual: Giant green '✓ Done.' fills the frame, then cracks to reveal slide 4 still reading €71–73m in red
hook_alternatives.line: 'Done' is the most expensive word in your inbox.
hook_alternatives.why: Leads with the film's own motif and a counter-intuitive claim; the viewer who has been burned by an AI 'Done' recognises it in 2 s.

hook_alternatives.first_3s_visual: Split screen: left the email with ≠ cards at 8:57; right the same email with €74.6m = €74.6m and a 'Sent · every change reviewed' toast
hook_alternatives.line: Same morning. One of these was checked.
hook_alternatives.why: Shows proof and roadmap inside 3 s, which this cut lacks until 46 s, and still opens the loop of how the right side happened.

issues.evidence: Frame 1 is a grey email client with an 'ILLUSTRATION' tag, a cursor and two dark cards; no person, no motion beyond the cursor. In a feed this reads as a static UI screenshot.
issues.suggested_action: Open on the real laptop/hands footage (already used at 8-10 s) with the ≠ cards composited on its screen, so frame 1 has a human and real light.

issues.evidence: Nothing in the first 45 s signals that a solution is coming; the logo appears only at f_19 (45 s).
issues.suggested_action: Add a 1-line promise in the cold open (e.g. super 'Here's how slide 4 slipped, and how to catch it') or a 0.5 s flash-forward of the real Changes panel before the rewind.

issues.evidence: Night grade dims the illustrated UI: the '✓ Done.' at 12 s is mid-grey on grey; 'Generating presentation… 16%' at 25 s is barely readable; the '8:45 MEETING AT 9:00' clock overlaps the 'You' avatar.
issues.suggested_action: Lift the key text ('Done.', the clock, the progress line) out of the grade so it stays near-white; move the clock clear of the sidebar avatar.

issues.evidence: The VO 'And the deck doesn't match the model' is concrete, but the ≠ cards are static and small next to the email; nothing moves toward a consequence.
issues.suggested_action: Animate the cursor actually pressing toward Send and freeze it 2 px away as the ≠ hits, so the stakes are an action about to happen.

issues.evidence: f_10 and f_13 show the same head-in-hands shot (same framing, map wall, pose).
issues.suggested_action: Replace the second use with a different reaction (the scratch-head clip the description promises) or cut it.

top_revision: Open on the real laptop with her hand on the trackpad and the €74.6m ≠ €71–73m cards on its screen, plus a one-line promise that the film will show how it gets caught, instead of a flat illustrated email.
